newsitem.title: USA: GATX CEO sees 1996 EPS flat with 1995.
newsitem.headline: GATX CEO sees 1996 EPS flat with 1995.

text.p: GATX Corp expects to post 1996 earnings that will be flat to a litttle bit up from 1995's, chief executive officer Ronald Zech told an analysts meeting in Chicago on Tuesday.

Excess industry capacity has hurt demand for the company's liquid storage systems business, which will post operating earnings of about half of last year's approximately $30 million, Zech told Reuters after his presentation.
"GATX's earnings (per share in 1996) will be in the same general range as last year," he said.
In 1995, GATX posted fully diluted per-share earnings of $4.13.

Zech said GATX Terminals Corp, the company's bulk liquid storage unit, has trimmed its headcount by 10 percent and will make further staff cuts. He sees the unit's 1,100 workforce being narrowed to about 900.
GATX, which leases tank and railcars, leases aircraft, handles 25 percent of the tonnage moved on the Great Lakes and runs a logistics business, employs a total of 6,000 workers.

Actions GATX is taking in its terminals and pipelines sector include aggressive cost control, locking in market share and building broad-based strategic customer relationships instead of regional relationships.
He also said the company would seek to broaden its international business.
Zech said the outlook for rail tank car demand is at record high levels and GATX's prospects remain solid in this core business.
